To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a low current operation is achieved by using a Ti nanofilm to form a W/TO/TaOx structure, where the Ti nanofilm is found to control the oxygen ion migration at the W/TiO interface.
the Ti nanolayer is found to control the oxygen ion migration at the W/TiO/Ox interface, and it is found to lead a good resistive memory performance with high density.

the resistive switching characteristics of W/TiO/W structure are significantly improved with a Ti nanolayers at the W/TiO/TaOx interfaces, and a conducting nanofilament is estimated to be approximately 3 nm in diameter by a new method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the resistive switching mechanism and memory characteristics of W/TiO/TaOx structure with a small size of 150 nm.
the development of a new resistive switching memory device with excellent memory properties.
the resistive switching memory device with high endurance, long read pulse lifetime, good data retention, and a small size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ti layer at the W/TiO/O/W structure can be used as a charge trap layer to enhance the switching stability, which could be used to develop a new generation of resistive switching memory.
a W/Ti/TaOx/Ti/W structure is proposed to achieve a low current operation with good memory characteristics and mechanism.

the presence of Ti nanolayer can effectively control oxygen ion (negative charge carrier) migration at the W/TiOxin/TaOxinterface, leading to enhanced resistive switching memory device characteristics and mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxygen ion migration is controlled by the Ti nanolayer.
the Ti nanolayer plays a critical role in controlling the filament formation and rupture, which leads to a low current operation and good resistive memory characteristics.
the Ti nanolayer could enhance the memory characteristics of the resistive random access memory (RRAM) by controlling the oxygen ion migration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ti nanolayer is effective in controlling the switching characteristics of the W/Ta2O5/TiO2/W structure.
the oxygen ion migration and filament formation/ruptures are controlled by a Ti nanolayers at the W/TiO/O interface, leading to a low current operation with good memory characteristics.
the Ti layer is an effective way to control the switching characteristics and mechanism, which can be applied in other metal oxide-based RRAMs.
